newsitem.title: USA: Ex-ConAgra managers plead guilty in case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-ConAgra managers plead guilty in case.

text.p: Four former ConAgra Inc managers agreed to plead guilty to criminal charges related to a grain handling case, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said Wednesday.

Earlier, Omaha, Neb.-based ConAgra said it agreed to pay $8.3 million and pleaded guilty to charges related to mishandling of grain. The charges were brought against Peavey Co, a ConAgra independent operating company.

The USDA said the $8.3 million settlement included a criminal fine of $4.4 million, a reimbursement of $450,000 to the USDA for unearned storage payments and expenses associated with the investigation, and about $3.45 million as compensation for criminal profits.
This penalty is in addition to an earlier civil settlement of more than $2.0 million that was reached between ConAgra and a group of Indiana farmers.
ConAgra said no one charged in this case works for it or Peavey today.
